- Model consistently overestimates prices, especially in early forecast periods (first 5–10 days of 30d window).
- Forecasts tend to peak too early or overshoot after sharp price spikes in history (e.g., 76+ in 2024-06-26).
- Model underestimates prices in late forecast periods (last 5–10 days of 30d), suggesting mean reversion bias or lagged response.
- Forecasts show persistent downward bias after mid-2024, particularly when true prices dip below 65–68.
- Model fails to capture sharp downward corrections after high peaks (e.g., 73+ → 65+ in 2024-09-06).
- Forecasts often lag true price movements by 2–5 days, especially in downward trends.
- Model exhibits “overfitting to recent highs” — forecasts rise with recent history even when true prices are falling.
- When history includes a strong downward trend, model tends to underestimate the depth of the drop.
- Model underestimates volatility in early periods but overestimates it in late periods — inconsistent variance capture.
- Forecasts should be adjusted downward by 2–5% for periods with recent sharp declines or high volatility.
